headline_marked: Hridoy's record fifty, Shakib's wicket [[Jaffna Kings reach LPL final]]
headline: Hridoy's record fifty, Shakib's wicket Jaffna Kings reach LPL final
summary: Tawhid Hridoy smashed the fastest fifty of the season, while Shakib Al Hasan's crucial breakthrough helped Jaffna Kings secure a 12-run win over Galle Gallants.
details: Tawhid Hridoy blazed an unbeaten 54 off just 21 balls, reaching his half-century in only 20 deliveries—the fastest fifty of the 2026 Lanka Premier League (LPL) season.
His explosive cameo, featuring three fours and five sixes, helped Jaffna Kings amass a record-breaking 242 for two, the highest team total in LPL history.
Opener Kamil Mishara also starred, scoring an unbeaten 108 off 55 balls with 10 fours and seven sixes.
In response, Galle Gallants fought back with contributions from Sam Harper (44) and Chamika Karunaratne (39), threatening to stay in the contest.
Shakib Al Hasan delivered a critical breakthrough in the 14th over by removing Karunaratne, halting Galle's momentum and tilting the match in Jaffna's favor.
Galle ended on 230 for eight, falling 12 runs short of the target. Mohamed Shiraz claimed three for 34, while Lizaad Williams took two wickets.
With this victory, Jaffna Kings have reached the final for the fifth time in six editions of the tournament since 2020.
Galle Gallants remain in contention and will face the loser of the eliminator between Colombo Kaps and Kandy Royals in Friday's second qualifier.
caption:
A record-breaking total and the fastest fifty of the season! 🏏

Tawhid Hridoy blazed an unbeaten 54 off just 21 balls, reaching his half-century in only 20 deliveries—the fastest fifty of the 2026 Lanka Premier League (LPL) season.

His explosive cameo, featuring three fours and five sixes, helped Jaffna Kings amass a record-breaking 242 for two, the highest team total in LPL history.

Opener Kamil Mishara also starred, scoring an unbeaten 108 off 55 balls with 10 fours and seven sixes.

In response, Galle Gallants fought back with contributions from Sam Harper (44) and Chamika Karunaratne (39), threatening to stay in the contest.

Shakib Al Hasan delivered a critical breakthrough in the 14th over by removing Karunaratne, halting Galle's momentum and tilting the match in Jaffna's favor.

Galle ended on 230 for eight, falling 12 runs short of the target. Mohamed Shiraz claimed three for 34, while Lizaad Williams took two wickets.

With this victory, Jaffna Kings have reached the final for the fifth time in six editions of the tournament since 2020.

Galle Gallants remain in contention and will face the loser of the eliminator between Colombo Kaps and Kandy Royals in Friday's second qualifier.

headline_marked: Landslides in Cox's Bazar: [[Rohingya child killed]] in refugee camp
headline: Landslides in Cox's Bazar: Rohingya child killed in refugee camp
summary: Torrential rain triggered multiple landslides in Ukhiya and on the Marine Drive, leading to one death and significant traffic disruptions.
details: A seven-year-old Rohingya child, identified as Nunushi, was killed today when earth collapsed on him at Block F-5 of Camp 13 in Tajnimarkhola, Ukhiya.
The landslide occurred around noon after continuous rainfall since last night weakened the hillside, burying the child under soil. He died on the spot.
Members of the 8th Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and local residents conducted a rescue operation. Families in high-risk areas have been advised to relocate to safer places.
In separate incidents, two landslides struck the Marine Drive road in the Darianagar area at 10:00 am and noon, halting traffic.
Army personnel were deployed to clear the debris from the road, allowing traffic to resume shortly after.
The Cox's Bazar Meteorological Office recorded 121mm of rainfall in the 24 hours leading up to noon today and predicts rain will continue for another three to four days.
caption:
A 7-year-old Rohingya child has been killed after landslides struck Cox's Bazar following torrential rains.

A seven-year-old Rohingya child, identified as Nunushi, was killed today when earth collapsed on him at Block F-5 of Camp 13 in Tajnimarkhola, Ukhiya.

The landslide occurred around noon after continuous rainfall since last night weakened the hillside, burying the child under soil. He died on the spot.

Members of the 8th Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and local residents conducted a rescue operation. Families in high-risk areas have been advised to relocate to safer places.

In separate incidents, two landslides struck the Marine Drive road in the Darianagar area at 10:00 am and noon, halting traffic.

Army personnel were deployed to clear the debris from the road, allowing traffic to resume shortly after.

The Cox's Bazar Meteorological Office recorded 121mm of rainfall in the 24 hours leading up to noon today and predicts rain will continue for another three to four days.
